title: Mittag-Leffler for Hom from a constant perfect reduction model
statement: Let X be a scheme, A a commutative Noetherian ring and J an ideal. Let U be affine and weakly contractible on the coefficient-sized pro-etale slice, in the precise sense of [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons]. Let P be a bounded finite-projective A-cochain complex, T=(B_X tensor_A P)|U and M in D(B_X|U) be locally complete. Suppose R_n(T) and R_n(M) are isomorphic for every n, without compatible choices. Then the actual Hom tower G_n=Hom(R_n(T),R_n(M)), with the normalized conjugated scalar-extension transitions of [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons], is Mittag-Leffler.

source.place: Tags 09C5 and 09C6, dual-perfect tensor calculation and exact sections on each affine weakly contractible covering object.

proof.text: Write B=B_X|U and T=B tensor_A P. The bounded finite-projective dual P^vee has degree-i term Hom_A(P^(-i),A) and differential (-1)^(i+1) times precomposition. Put H=(B tensor_A P^vee) tensor_B^L M. Finite-projective terms are idempotent summands of finite free terms; hence they are flat, and their tensor commutes with products and kernels. Boundedness makes the total dual complex K-flat and gives finite sums in every degree. Tensor the quotient-completion Roos triangle of M with this dual. Its products commute with this tensor, so H is the derived limit of its normalized reductions H_n=T_n^vee tensor^L M_n and is complete. Restriction to constant coefficients preserves those units and reductions. The individually given isomorphisms M_n isomorphic to T_n make each H_n a constant perfect complex. No compatibility of those isomorphisms is needed.

Weak contractibility makes evaluation on the slice exact. A free coefficient sheaf is projective there because its Hom is evaluation, and its finite direct summands are projective. The bounded projective complex T_n is K-projective. The derived-Hom bijection and finite-projective evaluation formula lambda tensor m sent to (p sent to lambda(p)m) identify H^0(U,H_n) with Hom(T_n,M_n). The dual signs and the tensor balancing formula commute with quotient maps, so the identifications respect the actual successor transitions in the statement, including both scalar-reassociation conjugations. Apply the constant-reductions Mittag-Leffler theorem to the complete restriction of H to constant A-coefficients: its residue constant value is perfect, and every reduction is independently constant. Transfer its Mittag-Leffler conclusion through those transition-compatible Hom identifications.

theorem adicResidueHomTower_mittagLeffler
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (J : Ideal A) (U : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X)
    (_hAffine : IsAffine
      ((AsSmall.down : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X ⥤ X.ProEt).obj U).left)
    (_hU : AdicResidueSliceWeaklyContractible.{u, v} X U)
    (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A) ℤ) (c d : ℤ)
    (_hc : P.IsStrictlyGE c) (_hd : P.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (_hP : ∀ q : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X q) ∧ Module.Projective A (P.X q))
    (M : AdicResidueLocalDerived.{u, v} X J U)
    (_hM : CategoryTheory.ConstantCompletion.IsComplete
      (adicResidueLocalProjection.{u, v} X J U 0) M)
    (_hfinite : ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty
      ((adicResidueLocalReduction.{u, v} X J U n).obj
        ((adicResidueRestriction
      (CategoryTheory.ConstantCompletion.completed (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X)
        A J) U).obj (adicResidueConstantPerfect.{u, v} X J P)) ≅
        (adicResidueLocalReduction.{u, v} X J U n).obj M)) :
    (adicResidueHomTower.{u, v} X J U
      ((adicResidueRestriction
      (CategoryTheory.ConstantCompletion.completed (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X)
        A J) U).obj (adicResidueConstantPerfect.{u, v} X J P)) M).IsMittagLeffler
